item.title: Site Dossier Help: Re: Site Dossier Help
item.content:encoded: As a general note, it's considered common courtesy to let authors know if you're going to reference their work in a piece you're writing. Both to make sure they're not unpleasantly caught off-guard if they see the crosslink, and to potentially get suggestions on how to correctly portray their content.

item.title: Site Dossier Help: Re: Site Dossier Help

item.title: Site Dossier Help: Re: Site Dossier Help
item.content:encoded: You're able to, yes. Authors tend to use site dossiers as little hubs for their articles that take place in the same setting (a surprisingly common gimmick) but if the vibe you're going for is helped by the inclusion of other articles then go for it.

item.content:encoded:
With that in mind, would the two be kept in the same SCP entry?

I would say yes, since the portal is the reason the being is now present on Earth, and that makes them inherently connected.

If SCP-X and SCP-Y were to be under the same entry, what would the Object Class at the top of the entry be?

Euclid. Consider the collective/total effort it would take to contain all aspects of the anomaly.

item.title: Labeling an SCP and determining its Object Class: Labeling an SCP and determining its Object Class
item.content:encoded:
Just some notes before I get into it:
1. Not entirely sure I am putting this thread in the right place since I have never posted on here before. If it is in the wrong place, I am sorry and could you please direct me to the right place?
2. I am not looking for a critique on the SCP I am writing. It is extremely unlikely that I will ever post the page for the SCP because I have no confidence and I just like writing these for fun.

I have two questions I need answers and one may answer the other.
Here is the situation. What I am going to refer to as SCP-X is a large sphere-shaped object that can be used to open a dimensional portal. SCP-Y is a sentient being that has come through the portal from the other dimension. SCP-Y is the only known being that has crossed over. The Foundation does not know if there are more beings on the other side because the portal closed again before they could explore it, and they do not know how to reopen it. SCP-Y has no connection to SCP-X aside from coming through the portal opened up by SCP-X. With that in mind, would the two be kept in the same SCP entry?
If the answer is no, then ignore the rest of this. If the answer is yes, I have another question.
SCP-X is considered Safe. Just build a structure around it (since it is too big to move) and it won't do anything. SCP-Y is Euclid. It is a sentient and sapient being that needs the same basic needs as a human. It also does not like to be contained and may try and break out, but none of its abilities really make it any harder to contain than a normal human. If SCP-X and SCP-Y were to be under the same entry, what would the Object Class at the top of the entry be?

Thanks for any help.

item.title: Continuing an old idea of mine: Re: Continuing an old idea of mine
item.content:encoded:
if I can't contact him, could I continue writing the idea without him?

I personally feel like the common courtesy thing to do would be to not continue writing the article if it was meant to be a co-authored piece. Worst case scenario would be that you write the piece, submit it to the site, and your co-author returns and is upset with the page and wants it taken down/rewritten.

Unless you agreed ahead of time what you would do if one of you had to leave the collaboration, it's probably best to work on something else. Respect for the absent and all that.

item.title: Continuing an old idea of mine: Re: Continuing an old idea of mine
item.content:encoded: i dont really see the problem with continuing on your own

item.title: Continuing an old idea of mine: Continuing an old idea of mine
item.content:encoded:
So about a year and a half ago, I got an idea greenlit for an SCP. At the time, I was sort of overwhelmed and I didn't feel I was a good enough writer to actually finish the draft for it by myself, so I reached out and got a co-author. We never really ended up finishing the draft because of personal life for me. On top of that, my co-author disappeared himself and hasn't done anything on the site since the time we got interrupted in July of 2019. I'm currently in the process of trying to contact him, but I don't have very much hope as our only method of communication was this site.

Now it's been a year and a half, so I'm certainly willing to go through the process of being greenlit again. My main question is if I can't contact him, could I continue writing the idea without him? I'm a much better writer so I'm confident I could do it myself, and I'll still keep his name in my posts of course.

item.title: Question about formatting?: Re: Question about formatting?
item.content:encoded:
i was wondering if I could add a "Special Transportation Procedures (or Protocols)" section AFTER the containment procedures section?

There's nothing that says you can't, though readers may wonder why you don't just make a bullet-point list of transportation information in the containment procedures. Also, if the transportation information is heavily bogged down with logistical minutiae, readers might just lose interest in the material and skip that section entirely.

Would that take away from my rating?

It probably wouldn't cause an immediate downvote, but it might give readers either a confusing or negative impression of the piece if there doesn't seem to be a need to separate transportation information entirely.

item.title: Seeing page comment replies: Re: Seeing page comment replies
item.content:encoded: Wikidot doesn't have any automated notifications. Closest you could get is maybe setting up an RSS feed, or just checking the discussion threads manually via the list on your wikidot profile.
